title: 1949 Battelle–Wright Field contract on titanium-nickel alloys and Nitinol
summary: Jesse Michels tells of 1949 Battelle–Wright Field contract on titanium-nickel alloys and Nitinol, about 1949-1960s at Wright Field / Wright-Patterson, Ohio; Navy lab, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.
place_text: Wright Field / Wright-Patterson, Ohio; Navy lab

tellings.quote: In 1949 there is a contract between Battelle Memorial Institute and Wright Air Field which turns into Wright-Patterson which is where the wreckage the Roswell wreckage was rumored to be taken.
Wright Patterson had [music] a contract with Battel Memorial Institute in 1949 studying nickel titanium alloys
tellings.link_reason: The same 1949 contract between Wright Field and Battelle Memorial Institute to study nickel-titanium alloys.

as_told.title: 1949 Wright-Patterson contract with Battelle on nickel-titanium alloys

related.note: Both are the 1949 Battelle contract that led to Nitinol and is offered as Roswell evidence. This telling makes Los Alamos the other party, where the story says Wright Field.

plain: The podcast host Jesse Michels says that in 1949 a private research group, the Battelle Memorial Institute, signed a contract with Wright Field, an Air Force base in Ohio later called Wright-Patterson, to study metals made of titanium and nickel. He notes that Wright Field is where wreckage from Roswell, the 1947 New Mexico crash some say was a flying saucer, was rumored to be taken, and he ties this work to Nitinol, a so-called memory metal that springs back to its shape, developed later at a Navy lab. If true, it would hint that an everyday material came from studying crash debris.
